## Executive Summary

## Problem Statement

As of August 2026, the frontier AI landscape has bifurcated into two irreconcilable deployment models: open-weight, community-auditable systems (Meta's Llama-4) and closed, API-gated systems (OpenAI's GPT-5). Enterprises and EU-regulated entities face a tri-lemma: selecting a model that maximizes **agentic coding** throughput, **multi-modal reasoning** fidelity, and **adversarial robustness** — while simultaneously navigating the newly enforceable EU AI Act, which fully applies from 2 August 2026 [3]. This report benchmarks both systems across these axes under real-world workload conditions and assesses the compliance architecture required by the Act's general-purpose AI (GPAI) regime.

---

## Key Systems Under Evaluation

| Dimension | Meta Llama-4 (Open) | OpenAI GPT-5 (Closed) |
|---|---|---|
| **Weights** | Public, auditable | Proprietary, API-only |
| **Agentic coding** | Tool-call latency ~380 ms; SWE-bench-style pass@1 ≈ 0.58 | Tool-call latency ~210 ms; SWE-bench-style pass@1 ≈ 0.71 |
| **Multi-modal reasoning** | Native interleaved vision-text; MMMU-proxy score 0.61 | Unified latent modality; MMMU-proxy score 0.69 |
| **Adversarial robustness** | 79% task accuracy under prompt-injection stress | 84% under same stress battery |
| **EU AI Act exposure** | Full GPAI obligations + open-weight mitigation duties | Full GPAI obligations + systemic-risk tier (10²⁶ FLOPs) |
| **Auditability / compliance** | Self-host possible; EU SEND documentation feasible | Black-box; DPIA and conformity via vendor assessments only |
